topic: BIOS and UEFI settings: boot order, secure boot, TPM, virtualisation
title: Prepare the firmware for a Windows 11 install
instructions:
## The installer will not start

A new PC must boot the Windows 11 installer from a USB stick, and the owner will run virtual machines on it later. Windows 11 refuses to install without **Secure Boot** and a **TPM 2.0**; a modern install also wants the SATA controller in **AHCI** mode.

## Do this

Set the firmware so that: the USB stick is first in the boot order, Secure Boot is enabled, the TPM is enabled, the SATA mode is AHCI, and CPU virtualisation (SVM / VT-x) is enabled. Leave Fast Boot off until the install has finished so the keyboard works in the installer.

settings.label: Boot Option #1
settings.help: The first device the firmware tries.

settings.label: Secure Boot
settings.help: Only signed boot loaders may run.

hints: Secure Boot cannot be enabled while the CSM (legacy mode) is on; disable the CSM first.
Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot; the installer checks both.
Fast Boot skips USB initialisation, which is why keyboards sometimes do not work in the installer.

checks.label: USB installer first in the boot order
Fast Boot off during the install

realityNote: Every vendor arranges these menus differently and names them differently (SVM on AMD, VT-x on Intel; fTPM versus PTT). Changing the SATA mode after an operating system is installed can make it unbootable, so set it before installing.
